motivating_context: S20 H1 (docs/research/s20_ob_oi_patient_runner) is the only route in this project's 46 prior tests with genuine edge that survived to the validation gate: development base PF 1.066 (137 fills), validation base PF 1.117 (43 fills) -- both real passes -- but validation STRESS PF 0.857, below the 1.00 gate, is the single reason it was REJECTED_AT_VALIDATION_GATE rather than promoted. Stress costs (5/8/5/5 bps maker/taker/slippage/limit-penetration vs base 2/5/2/2) model wider effective spreads and worse fills, which are disproportionately a low-liquidity-hours phenomenon on crypto perps (thin order books outside the London/NY session, more limit-penetration, more adverse selection on stops). This protocol tests whether restricting S20 H1's identical entries to the highest-liquidity UTC hours recovers the stress-cost margin, without touching the entry/exit logic itself -- entries outside the tested window are simply dropped, nothing else changes.

hypotheses.entry_exit: Identical to S20 H1 in every respect (order block + OI confirmation regime/structure/flow, breakeven+chandelier exit, partial_r=1.5, trail_atr=2.5, target_r=8.0) EXCEPT a signal is only taken if its entry-bar close-time hour (UTC) falls in [07:00, 20:00) -- the combined London open through US market close window, excluding the thin late-US/Asian session.
Identical to H1 except the window is narrowed to [12:00, 17:00) UTC -- the core London/New York overlap, the single highest-liquidity stretch of the crypto trading day.

single_variable_isolated: Both hypotheses reuse S20 H1's entry/exit formula completely unmodified (imported, not reimplemented) and differ from S20 H1 and from each other only in which UTC hours a signal is allowed to fire. No entry/exit parameter differs from S20 H1's frozen defaults.

symbols.note: Identical to S20 -- reuses the exact same cached klines/funding/metrics archives, no new data source.

promotion_gates.development_to_validation: PF >1.05, net PnL >0, at least 40 fills
promotion_gates.validation_to_retrospective_evaluation: base PF >1.10, stress PF >=1.00, at least 20 base fills, at least 2/3 symbols net positive, no symbol >60% gross profit
promotion_gates.paper_to_live: at least 200 prospective candidates across three full frozen months, PF >=1.25 base and >=1.10 stress, expectancy >=0.10R, 95% session-block bootstrap lower bound >0, max DD <=4%

execution.one_global_position: single global minute event loop with one shared cash balance, pending order and open position across the correlated ETH/SOL/BNB cluster
execution.ambiguous_bar: stop first; no favorable exit on limit fill minute

selection: Exactly H1 and H2. Session boundaries (07:00/20:00 UTC and 12:00/17:00 UTC) are standard, named market-session conventions chosen before any data was examined, not a scan over start/end hour combinations. A failing gate stops that route; choose no least-bad winner.
stress_semantics: Stress and severe are deployability replays: higher costs and limit penetration are known before entry, so the reward/cost filter is reapplied and the fill cohort may shrink.
known_limitations: Filtering necessarily reduces the fill count relative to S20 H1's own 137/43 development/validation fills -- both routes may fall below the 40-fill development minimum, a legitimate, disclosed possible outcome given S20 H1's fills were not evenly spread across all 24 hours to begin with; not grounds to widen the window afterward.

This is a filter, not a new signal: if it passes, the underlying edge is still the same fragile one S20 H1 already showed, now on a smaller, session-restricted sample -- a pass here raises rather than resolves the standard multiple-comparisons caution already flagged twice elsewhere in this project (S24->S28, S30 dev->validation).

Session boundaries are UTC calendar hours, not a true liquidity/spread measurement from order-book data (which this project does not reconstruct anywhere) -- a reasonable, standard proxy, disclosed as such.
This is a retrospective diagnostic; not a live paper-forward result unless it clears every gate through retrospective_evaluation.
